properties.name: Barrington Elementary School
properties.linked_campuses: Guerrero Thompson Elementary (75% of students, by address; inherits turnaround plan); Wooldridge Elementary (25%, by address)
properties.future_use: Swing campus for Wooldridge ES during modernization, then repurposing (ground lease scored highest; staff recommendation and board action still pending as of Sept 2026).
properties.reason: Chronically failing TEA ratings (closure/reassignment chosen as the state-approved turnaround option), declining enrollment and district budget deficit.
properties.plan_history: On the Oct 3, 2025 draft list of 13; retained Oct 31 (slice of Wooldridge zone returned to Wooldridge); on the Nov 4 phase-one list of 10; approved for closure Nov 20, 2025 on the 7-2 vote covering the seven F-rated campuses (Gonzales, de Urioste opposed). Last day May 28, 2026. Not declared surplus: building is swing space while Wooldridge ES is modernized (2022 bond); repurposing evaluation begun (long-term ground lease scored highest, 80/100; adaptive reuse w/ improvements 75, w/o 70, sale 60; survey open to Sept 15, 2026; staff recommendation pending). ~$4.9M of 2022 bond money already spent/committed (Austin Current, Jan 2026).
properties.community_response: Community meetings July 29 and August 2026; families cited the school as a hub for immigrant families (ballet folklorico, parent involvement).
properties.demographics_note: North Austin, opened 1969; 75%+ of students in bilingual education; large immigrant-family community (Statesman/Yahoo, May 2026). Three consecutive unacceptable TEA ratings; one of the 12 turnaround-plan campuses.

properties.name: Becker Elementary School
properties.linked_campuses: Galindo Elementary or Zilker Elementary (neighborhood students, by address); Sanchez Elementary (dual language program relocates as a two-way strand; Becker DL students get priority transfer)
properties.future_use: Adaptive reuse with improvements under district ownership; district to identify community/nonprofit partners in fall 2026.
properties.reason: Dual language program relocation to campuses with higher emergent-bilingual populations, declining enrollment and budget deficit.
properties.plan_history: Oct 3 draft: close, neighborhood to Zilker, DL program to Sanchez (Sanchez to become non-zoned). Oct 31: administration floated Galindo instead of Zilker. Final (Nov 14): students to Galindo or Zilker by address; Sanchez stays a neighborhood school with a DL strand. Closure approved Nov 20, 2025 on the 6-3 dual-language vote (Whitley Chu, Gonzales, de Urioste opposed). Last day May 28, 2026. Declared surplus June 18, 2026; board approved 'Adaptive Reuse with Improvements' (90/100; w/o improvements 80, ground lease 65, sale 50). Partner identification targeted for fall 2026.
properties.community_response: Parents wore protest shirts and testified against closure; dual-language advocates said the changes amounted to program elimination; the 1989 Green Classroom was cited as a loss.
properties.demographics_note: Bouldin Creek, South Austin; opened 1936, one of the district's oldest operating elementaries; school-wide (wall-to-wall) Spanish dual language program; volunteer-run Green Classroom since 1989. Not a turnaround campus.

properties.name: Dawson Elementary School
properties.linked_campuses: Galindo Elementary (100% of students; Galindo inherits Dawson's turnaround plan)
properties.future_use: To be sold (fee simple sale approved June 18, 2026; RFP issued).
properties.reason: Chronically failing TEA ratings (closure chosen as turnaround option), low enrollment, budget deficit.
properties.plan_history: Oct 3 draft: close and merge with Galindo; unchanged through Oct 31 and Nov 14. Approved Nov 20, 2025 (7-2). Last day May 28, 2026. Declared surplus June 18, 2026; district campus page says board approved 'Fee Simple Sale' (announcement wording: 'Fee Simple Sale or Long-Term Ground Lease'; both scored 85, adaptive reuse w/ improvements 75, w/o 65). RFP for the property has been released. Proceeds count toward the ~$60M one-time real-estate revenue assumed in the 2026-27 budget.
properties.community_response: Community described the school as a public/community space with intergenerational traditions; March 9 and May 13, 2026 repurposing meetings.
properties.demographics_note: South Austin, opened 1950s; ~80% economically disadvantaged (78.3% per state data), 26% English learners, 77% Hispanic; three consecutive unacceptable TEA ratings (turnaround campus). Laura Bush was its librarian in the 1970s.

properties.name: Oak Springs Elementary School
properties.linked_campuses: Blackshear Elementary (100% of students for 2026-27 and fall 2027 while Oak Springs is rebuilt; Blackshear inherits the turnaround plan)
properties.future_use: Rebuilt $47.6M campus reopens January 2028 as the combined Oak Springs/Blackshear school with a 'new shared identity'.
properties.reason: Chronically failing TEA ratings (closure/reassignment as turnaround option); building closes while the bond-funded rebuild continues.
properties.plan_history: Oct 3 draft: close and merge into Blackshear. Nov 14: district said Oak Springs/Blackshear construction continuation still under consideration. Approved for closure Nov 20, 2025 (7-2). Mid-Dec 2025: superintendent to decide by late January whether the merged school stays at Blackshear or moves to a rebuilt Oak Springs. March 30, 2026: announced Blackshear will close and both communities move into the modernized Oak Springs campus in January 2028. Last day May 28, 2026.
properties.community_response: Alumni nostalgia mixed with acceptance ('I hate to see it being closed but I know it is going to be rebuilt' - Constable Tonya Nixon); Blackshear parents raised concerns about a mid-year 2028 move under turnaround requirements.
properties.demographics_note: East Austin, opened 1958, serves the Booker T. Washington housing complex; three consecutive unacceptable TEA ratings (turnaround campus). $47.6M 2022-bond modernization (about $48M spent/committed per Austin Current).

properties.name: Ridgetop Elementary School
properties.linked_campuses: Reilly Elementary (all neighborhood students); Pickle Elementary (dual language program relocates as a two-way strand; priority transfers)
properties.future_use: Adaptive reuse under district ownership with community partners; parents proposed a walkable community center keeping the playground open.
properties.reason: Dual language program consolidation, declining enrollment, budget deficit.
properties.plan_history: Oct 3 draft: close, neighborhood to Reilly, DL to Pickle (Pickle to go non-zoned). Final Nov 14: Pickle stays a neighborhood school with a DL strand. Approved Nov 20, 2025 on the 6-3 dual-language vote. Last day May 28, 2026. Declared surplus June 18, 2026; board approved 'Adaptive Reuse with or without Improvements' (both 85/100; ground lease 65, sale 45). Partner identification targeted for fall 2026.
properties.community_response: Parents proposed a community center; school traditions and a 30-year principal were cited; March 24 and May 19, 2026 repurposing meetings.
properties.demographics_note: North Loop; small, high-performing school with a pioneering wall-to-wall Spanish-English dual language program. Not a turnaround campus.

properties.name: Sunset Valley Elementary School
properties.address: 3000 Jones Rd, Austin (City of Sunset Valley), TX 78745
properties.linked_campuses: Boone Elementary or Cunningham Elementary (neighborhood students, by address); Odom Elementary (dual language program relocates; Odom becomes the district's only non-zoned school-wide DL campus)
properties.future_use: To be sold outright (fee simple sale approved June 18, 2026); prioritized for monetization toward the ~$60M real-estate revenue target.
properties.reason: Dual language program consolidation, declining enrollment, budget deficit.
properties.plan_history: Oct 3 draft: close, DL to Odom, neighborhood mostly to Cunningham. Oct 31: larger share reassigned to Boone. Final: Boone or Cunningham by address. Approved Nov 20, 2025 (6-3). Last day May 28, 2026. Declared surplus June 18, 2026; Fee Simple Sale approved (95/100; ground lease 80, adaptive reuse 75/75).
properties.community_response: Teachers reported students 'very sad, very worried'; parent Zoe Trieff: 'this is the first domino that is falling.'
properties.demographics_note: Opened 1971; the only school inside the City of Sunset Valley; school-wide dual language program. Not a turnaround campus.

properties.name: Widén Elementary School
properties.linked_campuses: Rodriguez Elementary (100% of students; inherits turnaround plan)
properties.future_use: Adaptive reuse under district ownership; partner identification targeted for fall 2026; city exploring public-benefit partnership.
properties.reason: Chronically failing TEA ratings (closure as turnaround option), budget deficit.
properties.plan_history: Oct 3/Oct 31 drafts: split between Rodriguez and Houston by address. Final (Nov 14): all students to Rodriguez, to avoid placing students in another failing school. Approved Nov 20, 2025 (7-2; Winn/Widén turnaround plans passed 5-4). Last day May 28, 2026. Declared surplus June 18, 2026; 'Adaptive Reuse Without Improvements' approved (85/100; w/ improvements 75, ground lease 70, sale 50). Council Member Fuentes's March 2026 resolution named Widén for a possible city partnership.
properties.community_response: Community emphasized the school as a basic-needs hub; City Council directed the city manager to develop a land policy on closing sites by June 1, 2026.
properties.demographics_note: Dove Springs; ~83% economically disadvantaged; anchors a cluster of library, recreation and health centers; three consecutive unacceptable TEA ratings (turnaround campus). ~$2.8M bond money spent/committed.

properties.name: Winn Montessori School
properties.linked_campuses: Andrews Elementary (80% of neighborhood students, by address; inherits turnaround plan); Pecan Springs Elementary (20%, by address); Reilly Elementary (Montessori program relocates as a strand; priority transfers)
properties.future_use: Swing campus during the Andrews ES rebuild, then repurposing (recommendation pending).
properties.reason: Chronically failing TEA ratings (closure as turnaround option), budget deficit.
properties.plan_history: Oct 3 draft: close; neighborhood to Andrews/Hart/Pecan Springs; Montessori to Govalle as a non-zoned campus. Oct 29 workshop: trustees asked for alternatives (Zavala/Ortega floated). Final (Nov 14): Montessori moves to Reilly; students to Andrews or Pecan Springs. Approved Nov 20, 2025 (7-2; turnaround plan 5-4). Last day May 28, 2026. Building is now the swing campus while Andrews ES is modernized (2022 bond); repurposing evaluation under way (ground lease scored highest 75/100; adaptive reuse 70/65, sale 70; survey to Sept 15, 2026; staff recommendation pending).
properties.community_response: Families called the Reilly move 'geographically prohibitive'; community meeting July 28, 2026 and a second in August.
properties.demographics_note: Northeast Austin; the district's only Montessori school; three consecutive unacceptable TEA ratings (turnaround campus).

properties.name: Bedichek Middle School
properties.linked_campuses: Covington Middle School (58% of students; inherits turnaround plan); Paredes Middle School (23%; Paredes itself closed July 30, 2026, so those students were re-routed to Bailey or Mendez); Mendez Middle School (13%)
properties.future_use: Building kept as a district facility (SpEd offices, training, 18+ program, community partners); surplus land to be ground-leased via RFP.
properties.reason: Chronically failing TEA ratings (closure as turnaround option), budget deficit.
properties.plan_history: Oct 3 draft: 'temporary' closure, students to Covington/Paredes/Lively/Mendez. Oct 31: Lively share redirected to Mendez; PK-8 or 6-12 DL reopening floated. Final: Covington, Paredes or Mendez by address. Approved Nov 20, 2025 (7-2). Last day May 28, 2026. Building 'land banked' (kept): Special Education Dept offices, districtwide professional learning, 18+ special-education programming, community partners. Adjacent surplus land declared surplus June 18, 2026 with a long-term ground lease approved (90/100; sale 85); RFP process under way. The July 2026 Paredes closure re-routed former Bedichek students who had been zoned to Paredes.
properties.community_response: Alumni loyalty; community meetings April 7 and June 4, 2026.
properties.demographics_note: Opened 1972; only middle-school JROTC in the district; top AVID program; 'Dazed and Confused' filming site; three consecutive unacceptable TEA ratings (turnaround campus). ~$1.2M bond money spent.

properties.name: Martin Middle School
properties.enrollment_prior: More than 500 students in 2018-19; 240 in April 2025 (KXAN)
properties.linked_campuses: Kealing Middle School (61% of students; inherits turnaround plan); Lively Middle School (26%); Dr. General Marshall Middle School (13%)
properties.future_use: Kept by district for a to-be-determined educational use (land bank); community floated a multipurpose school-plus-community-center model with adult education.
properties.reason: Chronically failing TEA ratings (closure as turnaround option), low enrollment, budget deficit.
properties.plan_history: Oct 3 draft: 'temporary' closure, students to Kealing/Lively/Marshall; Garza Independence HS proposed to move into the building as a 6-12 school (removed from the final draft after outcry, though the Nov 14 plan still said Garza relocation could be considered 'not before 2026-27'). Approved Nov 20, 2025 (7-2). Last day May 28, 2026. Retained as a 'land bank' property; the 2022 bond modernization was suspended mid-project and is resuming at a limited scope for preservation; community meeting July 14, 2026 and survey; future use tied to a districtwide academic visioning process.
properties.community_response: East Austin neighbors want it to stay a community hub; public meeting and survey.
properties.demographics_note: East Austin on Lady Bird Lake; opened 1967; first fully integrated AISD campus; three consecutive unacceptable TEA ratings (turnaround campus). $36.5M of 2022 bond modernization already spent/committed.

properties.name: International High School
properties.address: 7104 Berkman Dr, Austin, TX 78752 (co-located at Northeast Early College HS)
properties.enrollment_prior: 213 (2024-25) to 95 (2025-26) per Statesman; only 9 freshmen enrolled in Aug 2025 (~90% drop)
properties.linked_campuses: Northeast Early College High School (host campus; current students may stay through graduation with district transportation); Zoned home high schools (new students, with 'specialized newcomer support')
properties.reason: Low enrollment.
properties.plan_history: Oct 3 draft: close the stand-alone campus and continue as a program at Navarro ECHS. Final (Nov 14): Navarro program dropped; school closes, students return to zoned campuses with newcomer support. Approved Nov 20, 2025. December 2025 letter to families: current students may remain at Northeast through graduation with transportation, or enroll at their zoned campus.
properties.demographics_note: Serves 9th-10th grade newcomer/multilingual immigrant students; enrollment collapse attributed to immigration-related fears.

properties.name: Paredes Middle School
properties.address: 10100 S Mary Moore Searight Dr, Austin, TX 78748
properties.linked_campuses: Bedichek Middle School (was designated to receive 23% of Bedichek's zone in 2026-27); Bailey Middle School (about 55% of students; inherits the TEA-approved turnaround plan); Mendez Middle School (about 45%; students east of Bluff Springs Rd and north of Slaughter Ln)
properties.future_use: Not a school in 2026-27; landmark/repurpose evaluation pending.
properties.reason: Anticipated (later confirmed) fourth consecutive F rating and staffing vacancies; district amended its turnaround plan from 'restart' to 'reassignment' to give students stronger environments and avoid further state intervention.
properties.plan_history: Nov 20, 2025: designated a Bedichek receiving school and an ACE restart campus; interim principal Jordan Curtin confirmed Dec 10, 2025. July 22, 2026: superintendent proposed immediate closure; community sessions July 28-30; board voted 7-2 on July 30, 2026 (de Urioste, Quintana opposed) to close before the Aug 18 first day; no layoffs (staff reassigned, including to Bailey and Mendez); TEA approved the closure as a turnaround-plan amendment (reported Aug 13, 2026 alongside the fourth F). Bailey needs portable classrooms to absorb the students (Austin Current, Aug 28). Building to be evaluated for landmarking or repurposing.
properties.community_response: Parents criticized the abrupt timeline weeks before school started and asked whether east-of-I-35 demographics drove the decision.
properties.demographics_note: Southeast Austin; three consecutive F ratings then a fourth (preliminary Aug 2026); 'district-managed restart' (ACE model) campus in the Nov 2025 plan, turnaround plan approved by TEA January 2026; most staff vacancies of any AISD school (superintendent).

properties.name: Blackshear Elementary School (Fine Arts Academy)
properties.linked_campuses: Oak Springs Elementary (receives 100% of Oak Springs students for 2026-27 and fall 2027; merged school moves to new Oak Springs campus January 2028)
properties.future_use: Closes January 2028; historic designation sought; district retains the building and will seek monetization/community options with community input.
properties.reason: Receives all Oak Springs students while Oak Springs is rebuilt; then consolidates into the new $47.6M Oak Springs building (district decision March 30, 2026).
properties.plan_history: Oct 3 draft: receiving campus for Oak Springs with boundary changes (dropped). Nov 14/20: Oak Springs students to Blackshear; district said Blackshear would 'likely close' when the new building opens. Mid-Dec 2025: decision promised by late January. March 30, 2026: superintendent announced Blackshear closes and both communities move to the modernized Oak Springs in January 2028; district to pursue historic designation and keep ownership while exploring monetization/community use. Community meeting on the building postponed to fall 2026 as 'insensitive' during the merger.
properties.community_response: Parents objected that a 'campus move' had become an acknowledged closure ('It is now officially a closure') and worried about capacity, the fine arts program, and a mid-year move under turnaround requirements.
properties.demographics_note: Opened 1891; historically Black East Austin school; fine arts academy; inherits Oak Springs's turnaround plan; required Targeted Improvement Plan.

properties.name: Galindo Elementary School
properties.linked_campuses: Dawson Elementary (100% of students); Becker Elementary (part, by address)
properties.reason: Receives all Dawson students and part of the Becker zone.
properties.plan_history: Oct 3: receive Dawson plus some Joslin students with boundary changes. Oct 29-31: proposal to send Becker zone to Galindo instead of Zilker. Final: receives Dawson and part of Becker; Joslin changes dropped. Principal Natascha Barreto-Romero confirmed Dec 10, 2025. Phase-1 boundary relief for receiving campuses planned for 2027-28.
properties.community_response: Trustees questioned moving students from F-rated to lower-rated campuses.
properties.demographics_note: Inherits Dawson's turnaround plan as the receiving campus.

properties.name: Zilker Elementary School
properties.linked_campuses: Becker Elementary (part, by address)
properties.reason: Receives part of the Becker attendance zone.
properties.plan_history: Oct 3: all Becker neighborhood students to Zilker. Oct 31: district floated shifting Becker zone to Galindo. Final: Becker split between Galindo and Zilker by address.

properties.name: Guerrero Thompson Elementary School
properties.linked_campuses: Barrington Elementary (75%)
properties.reason: Receives 75% of Barrington students.
properties.plan_history: Oct 3: receive Barrington plus a slice of Wooldridge; Oct 31: Wooldridge slice returned to Wooldridge due to building constraints. Final unchanged; principal Briana Garcia confirmed Dec 10, 2025.
properties.community_response: Barrington families raised staffing and program concerns.
properties.demographics_note: Inherits Barrington's turnaround plan; feeds Dobie MS.

properties.name: Wooldridge Elementary School
properties.linked_campuses: Barrington Elementary (25%)
properties.reason: Receives 25% of Barrington students.
properties.plan_history: Oct 3: receive some Barrington students with boundary changes; Oct 31: part of zone returned from Guerrero-Thompson (boundary changes later dropped). Restart plan approved Nov 20, 2025; new principal Nick Martinez (from Wooten) appointed Dec 10, 2025.
properties.demographics_note: Own three-F turnaround campus: 'district-managed restart' (ACE model) in 2026-27; campus being modernized with 2022 bond, using the Barrington building as swing space.

properties.name: Rodriguez Elementary School
properties.linked_campuses: Widén Elementary (100% of students)
properties.reason: Receives all Widén students.
properties.plan_history: Oct 3/31: receive part of Widén (rest to Houston). Final Nov 14: receives all Widén students. Principal Monica Mills confirmed Dec 10, 2025.
properties.demographics_note: Inherits Widén's turnaround plan.

properties.name: Reilly Elementary School
properties.linked_campuses: Ridgetop Elementary (all neighborhood students); Winn Montessori (Montessori program moves here); Wooten Elementary (Reilly dual language and Mandarin programs move there)
properties.reason: Program reshuffle: its school-wide dual language program ends (moves to Wooten), it absorbs Ridgetop's neighborhood and hosts the relocated Montessori program.
properties.plan_history: Oct 3: DL program to Wooten; receives Ridgetop neighborhood. Final Nov 14: same plus Montessori strand from Winn (instead of Govalle); Reilly DL students get priority transfers to other DL campuses. Approved Nov 20, 2025 (dual-language vote 6-3). Principal Leyla Olano moved to Wooten (Dec 10, 2025).
properties.community_response: Reilly DL families said the change amounted to program closure.
properties.demographics_note: Formerly a school-wide Spanish dual language campus with a Mandarin strand; becomes a neighborhood school with a Montessori strand. The building stays open; only the program 'closes'.

properties.name: Boone Elementary School
properties.linked_campuses: Sunset Valley Elementary (part, by address)
properties.reason: Receives part of Sunset Valley's attendance zone.
properties.plan_history: Oct 3: boundary changes only; Oct 31: larger share of Sunset Valley reassigned to Boone instead of Cunningham. Final: Sunset Valley students to Boone or Cunningham by address.

properties.name: Cunningham Elementary School
properties.linked_campuses: Sunset Valley Elementary (part, by address)
properties.reason: Receives part of Sunset Valley's attendance zone.
properties.plan_history: Oct 3: receive most Sunset Valley and some Joslin students; Oct 31: share reduced in favor of Boone; Joslin changes dropped. Final: Sunset Valley students to Boone or Cunningham.

properties.name: Andrews Elementary School
properties.linked_campuses: Winn Montessori (80%, by address)
properties.reason: Receives 80% of Winn Montessori's neighborhood students.
properties.plan_history: Oct 3: receive Winn students plus boundary changes (dropped Nov 4). Final: Winn students to Andrews or Pecan Springs. Principal Audrey Guerrero confirmed Dec 10, 2025.
properties.demographics_note: Inherits Winn's turnaround plan; campus being modernized (2022 bond) with the Winn building as swing space.

properties.name: Pecan Springs Elementary School
properties.linked_campuses: Winn Montessori (20%, by address)
properties.reason: Receives 20% of Winn Montessori's neighborhood students.
properties.plan_history: Oct 3: receive Winn students with small boundary changes (dropped). Restart plan approved Nov 20, 2025; new principal Paula Noe (from Maplewood) appointed Dec 10, 2025.
properties.demographics_note: Own three-F turnaround campus: district-managed restart (ACE model) 2026-27.

properties.name: Kealing Middle School
properties.linked_campuses: Martin Middle School (61%, by address)
properties.reason: Receives 61% of Martin's attendance zone.
properties.plan_history: Oct 3/31: receive Martin students plus boundary changes (dropped). Principal Tim Estes confirmed Dec 10, 2025.
properties.demographics_note: Inherits Martin's turnaround plan.

properties.name: Lively Middle School
properties.linked_campuses: Martin Middle School (26%, by address)
properties.reason: Receives 26% of Martin's attendance zone.
properties.plan_history: Oct 3: receive students from both Bedichek and Martin; Oct 31: Bedichek share redirected to Mendez. Final: receives Martin students only.

properties.name: Dr. General Marshall Middle School
properties.enrollment_prior: Opened 2023-24 with a single 6th-grade cohort drawn from eight elementary schools
properties.linked_campuses: Martin Middle School (13%, by address)
properties.reason: Receives 13% of Martin's attendance zone; Phase 1 of the boundary realignment (vote expected Oct 2026) will define its first attendance area for 2027-28.
properties.plan_history: Oct 3/31: new boundary drawn (districtwide boundaries dropped Nov 4). Final: receives Martin students. Boundary Phase 1 narrowed in Aug 2026 to Marshall MS and Linder ES: open houses Aug 29, Sept 14 and Sept 16, 2026; recommendations September; board vote October 2026; effective 2027-28.
properties.demographics_note: Mueller-area campus opened Oct 2023 (2017 bond); has never had a formal attendance boundary. Not in the GIS library.

properties.name: Covington Middle School
properties.linked_campuses: Bedichek Middle School (58%, by address)
properties.reason: Receives 58% of Bedichek's attendance zone.
properties.plan_history: Oct 3/31: receive Bedichek students plus boundary changes (dropped). Principal Cedric Maddox confirmed Dec 10, 2025.
properties.demographics_note: Inherits Bedichek's turnaround plan.

properties.name: Mendez Middle School
properties.linked_campuses: Bedichek Middle School (13%, by address); Paredes Middle School (about 45% of students, from Aug 2026)
properties.reason: Receives 13% of Bedichek's zone (2026-27) and, after the July 2026 Paredes closure, about 45% of Paredes students (east of Bluff Springs Rd and north of Slaughter Ln).
properties.plan_history: Oct 3: receive some Bedichek students; Oct 31: share increased (fewer to Lively). Final: Covington/Paredes/Mendez by address. July 30, 2026: designated receiver for Paredes students east of Bluff Springs Rd/north of Slaughter Ln.
properties.demographics_note: SB 1882 partnership campus; Oct 31 draft floated a possible future PK-8 at Mendez.

properties.name: Bailey Middle School
properties.linked_campuses: Paredes Middle School (about 55% of students; includes former Bedichek-zone students who had been assigned to Paredes)
properties.reason: Receives about 55% of Paredes students (all Paredes-zoned students not assigned to Mendez) after the July 2026 Paredes closure.
properties.plan_history: Not in the Nov 2025 closure plan (only boundary tweaks in the Oct drafts, dropped). Added July 30, 2026 as Paredes receiver; took on Paredes' turnaround plan; first day Aug 18, 2026.
properties.demographics_note: Inherited Paredes's TEA-approved turnaround plan in August 2026; needs portable classrooms to absorb the students (Austin Current, Aug 28, 2026).

properties.name: Sánchez Elementary School
properties.linked_campuses: Becker Elementary (dual language program and priority transfers)
properties.reason: Receives Becker's dual language program as a two-way strand (stays a neighborhood school).
properties.plan_history: Oct 3: become non-zoned school-wide Spanish DL campus, neighborhood to Allison/Zavala/Travis Heights. Final Nov 14: remains a neighborhood campus with a two-way DL strand. Restart plan approved Nov 20, 2025; principal Travis Barrett (from Becker) appointed Dec 10, 2025.
properties.demographics_note: Own three-F turnaround campus: district-managed restart (ACE model) 2026-27; higher emergent-bilingual population.

properties.name: Pickle Elementary School
properties.linked_campuses: Ridgetop Elementary (dual language program and priority transfers)
properties.reason: Receives Ridgetop's dual language program as a two-way strand (stays a neighborhood school).
properties.plan_history: Oct 3: become non-zoned school-wide DL, neighborhood to Hart. Final: neighborhood school with DL strand. Principal Kara Schultz (from Ridgetop) appointed Dec 10, 2025.

properties.name: Wooten Elementary School
properties.linked_campuses: Reilly Elementary (dual language and Mandarin programs)
properties.reason: Receives Reilly's Spanish dual language program (two-way strand) and Reilly's Mandarin dual-language program.
properties.plan_history: Oct 3: become non-zoned school-wide DL, neighborhood to Pillow. Oct 31: Mandarin continuation added. Final: neighborhood school with DL strand plus Mandarin. Principal Leyla Olano (from Reilly) appointed Dec 10, 2025.
properties.demographics_note: Recently modernized (2022 bond) campus.

properties.name: Odom Elementary School
properties.linked_campuses: Sunset Valley Elementary (dual language program and priority transfers); Pleasant Hill Elementary (receives Odom's neighborhood students)
properties.reason: Receives Sunset Valley's school-wide dual language program; converts to a non-zoned DL campus; Odom's neighborhood (English/ESL) students are reassigned to Pleasant Hill, with current 3rd/4th graders allowed to finish at Odom.
properties.plan_history: Oct 3/31: non-zoned school-wide DL, neighborhood to Pleasant Hill. Final Nov 14: confirmed as the one non-zoned DL campus; neighborhood reassignment to Pleasant Hill retained (KXAN/KVUE final-plan coverage). Approved Nov 20, 2025. Principal Elaine Navarro (from Sunset Valley) appointed Dec 10, 2025.
properties.demographics_note: Becomes the district's only campus-wide, non-zoned (open citywide) Spanish dual language school.

properties.name: Pleasant Hill Elementary School
properties.linked_campuses: Odom Elementary (neighborhood students reassigned here; Odom 3rd/4th graders in English/ESL classrooms may finish at Odom)
properties.reason: Receives Odom's neighborhood (non-dual-language) students when Odom becomes a non-zoned dual language campus.
properties.plan_history: In the Oct 3/Oct 31 drafts and retained in the Nov 14 final plan approved Nov 20, 2025.

properties.name: Blazier Elementary School
properties.reason: Sixth grade discontinued; rising 6th graders attend their zoned middle school.
properties.plan_history: In Oct 3 draft (no boundary change, drop 6th grade); retained in final plan and approved Nov 20, 2025.
properties.demographics_note: Blazier ES / Blazier Intermediate; feeds Paredes MS (now Bailey/Mendez after the Paredes closure).

properties.name: Mathews Elementary School
properties.reason: Sixth grade discontinued.
properties.plan_history: Oct 3: drop 6th grade and receive Bryker Woods students with boundary changes; Oct 31: Bryker Woods receivers shifted toward Brentwood/Casis; Nov 4: Bryker Woods closure and boundaries deferred. Final: 6th-grade removal only; approved Nov 20, 2025.

properties.name: Russell Lee Elementary School
properties.reason: Sixth grade discontinued.
properties.plan_history: In Oct 3 draft (no boundary change, drop 6th grade); retained in final plan; approved Nov 20, 2025.

properties.name: Palm Elementary School
properties.linked_campuses: Perez Elementary (proposed receiver in Oct 3/Oct 31 drafts)
properties.reason: Original reason: under-enrollment/boundary balancing; removed Nov 4, 2025 because it was 'not impacted by turnaround plans or the district's efforts to move its dual language programs'.
properties.plan_history: Oct 3 draft: close and merge into Perez. Nov 4, 2025: removed from the Nov 20 vote; to be reconsidered fall 2026. June/July 2026: district said it is 'suspending any additional school closures' and moved districtwide consolidation review to Phase 2 (planning from spring 2027, vote fall 2027, effective 2028-29), though the superintendent said Phase 2 'could also include more school closures'.
properties.community_response: Parents relieved but split on whether the delay was trustworthy.
properties.demographics_note: Southeast Austin; not a turnaround campus.

properties.name: Bryker Woods Elementary School
properties.linked_campuses: Mathews Elementary, Casis Elementary, Brentwood Elementary (proposed receivers by address, Oct 3/Oct 31 drafts)
properties.reason: Original reason: under-enrollment/boundary balancing; removed Nov 4, 2025 pending more engagement.
properties.plan_history: Oct 3 draft: close, students to Mathews/Casis/Brentwood. Oct 31: more students shifted to Brentwood and Casis. Nov 4: removed from vote; district later suspended additional closures pending Phase 2 (2028-29).
properties.demographics_note: Central/West Austin; not a turnaround campus.

properties.name: Maplewood Elementary School
properties.linked_campuses: Campbell Elementary (proposed receiver in Oct 3/Oct 31 drafts)
properties.reason: Original reason: under-enrollment/boundary balancing; removed Nov 4, 2025.
properties.plan_history: Oct 3 draft: close and merge into Campbell. Nov 4: removed from vote; district later suspended additional closures pending Phase 2. Principal Paula Noe moved to Pecan Springs (Dec 10, 2025).
properties.community_response: Maplewood parents questioned the process.
properties.demographics_note: East/Central Austin; not a turnaround campus.

properties.name: Govalle Elementary School
properties.linked_campuses: Winn Montessori (proposed program receiver, dropped); Ortega Elementary and Zavala Elementary (proposed receivers of Govalle neighborhood, dropped)
properties.reason: Oct 3 draft proposed converting Govalle into the district's non-zoned Montessori campus (neighborhood students to Ortega/Zavala); dropped after community protest; Montessori went to Reilly instead.
properties.plan_history: Oct 3: become non-zoned Montessori campus. Oct 29 workshop: trustees requested alternatives. Nov 14 final: Montessori to Reilly; Govalle unchanged.
properties.community_response: Govalle families protested the program transfer.
properties.demographics_note: Recently modernized building.

properties.name: Joslin Elementary School
properties.linked_campuses: Cunningham Elementary, Galindo Elementary, Zilker Elementary (proposed receivers of Joslin neighborhood, dropped)
properties.reason: Oct 3 draft proposed converting Joslin to a non-zoned Spanish and Mandarin immersion campus; the Nov 14 final plan left the idea 'under consideration' with no 2026-27 implementation, so it was not part of the Nov 20 vote.
properties.plan_history: Oct 3: non-zoned immersion program; Nov 14: decision pending, remains a neighborhood school for 2026-27.
properties.demographics_note: Has an existing Mandarin dual-language program.

properties.name: Garza Independence High School
properties.linked_campuses: Martin Middle School (proposed destination, dropped); Alternative Learning Center (proposed to take Garza's building, dropped)
properties.reason: Oct 3/Oct 31 drafts proposed relocating Garza into the Martin MS building as a 6-12 program (with the Alternative Learning Center moving into Garza's building); after protests the idea was removed from the final draft (KXAN), though the Nov 14 plan said relocation could still be considered 'not before 2026-27' (KUT). Not part of the Nov 20 approved actions; Martin was later land-banked with use TBD.
properties.plan_history: Proposal surfaced Oct 3, discussed Oct 29 workshop, protests early November; absent from the Nov 21, 2025 approved actions.
properties.community_response: Protest rally outside Garza; teachers petitioned against the move.
properties.demographics_note: Self-paced diploma-completion high school for at-risk students.

properties.name: Alternative Learning Center
properties.linked_campuses: Garza Independence High School (proposed building swap, dropped)
properties.reason: Oct drafts considered moving ALC into the Garza building; not carried into the approved plan.
properties.plan_history: Exploratory note in Oct 3/Oct 31 plan pages; absent from approved Nov 20, 2025 actions.

properties.name: Houston Elementary School
properties.linked_campuses: Widén Elementary (proposed partial receiver, dropped)
properties.reason: Was to receive part of Widén's zone in the Oct 3/Oct 31 drafts; the final plan sent all Widén students to Rodriguez to avoid placing them in another failing school.
properties.plan_history: Oct 3/31: receive some Widén students; Nov 14: removed.
properties.demographics_note: Failing-rated campus with a school-improvement plan.

properties.name: Perez Elementary School
properties.address: 7500 S Pleasant Valley Rd, Austin, TX
properties.linked_campuses: Palm Elementary (proposed feeder, deferred)
properties.reason: Proposed receiver for Palm Elementary in the Oct drafts; Palm closure deferred Nov 4, 2025.
properties.plan_history: Oct 3/31 drafts only.

properties.name: Campbell Elementary School
properties.linked_campuses: Maplewood Elementary (proposed feeder, deferred)
properties.reason: Proposed receiver for Maplewood Elementary in the Oct drafts; Maplewood closure deferred Nov 4, 2025.
properties.plan_history: Oct 3/31 drafts only (also boundary changes with Blackshear, dropped).

properties.name: Brentwood Elementary School
properties.linked_campuses: Bryker Woods Elementary (proposed feeder, deferred)
properties.reason: Proposed receiver for Bryker Woods students (share increased Oct 31); Bryker Woods closure deferred Nov 4, 2025.
properties.plan_history: Oct 3/31 drafts only.

properties.name: Casis Elementary School
properties.linked_campuses: Bryker Woods Elementary (proposed feeder, deferred)
properties.reason: Proposed receiver for Bryker Woods students; Bryker Woods closure deferred Nov 4, 2025.
properties.plan_history: Oct 3/31 drafts only.

properties.name: Hart Elementary School
properties.linked_campuses: Pickle Elementary (proposed feeder, dropped); Winn Montessori (proposed small feeder, dropped)
properties.reason: Oct drafts had Hart receive Pickle's whole neighborhood (Pickle to go non-zoned) and a small group from Winn; final plan kept Pickle zoned and sent Winn students to Andrews/Pecan Springs only.
properties.plan_history: Oct 3/31 drafts only.

properties.name: Pillow Elementary School
properties.linked_campuses: Wooten Elementary (proposed feeder, dropped)
properties.reason: Oct drafts had Pillow absorb Wooten's neighborhood (Wooten to go non-zoned); final plan kept Wooten as a neighborhood school.
properties.plan_history: Oct 3/31 drafts only.

properties.name: Allison Elementary School
properties.linked_campuses: Sánchez Elementary (proposed feeder, dropped)
properties.reason: Oct drafts had Allison absorb most Sánchez neighborhood students (Sánchez to go non-zoned); final plan kept Sánchez zoned.
properties.plan_history: Oct 3/31 drafts only.

properties.name: Ortega Elementary School
properties.linked_campuses: Govalle Elementary (proposed feeder, dropped)
properties.reason: Oct drafts: receive Govalle neighborhood students and considered as an alternative Montessori site; dropped when Montessori went to Reilly.
properties.plan_history: Oct 3/31 drafts only.

properties.name: Zavala Elementary School
properties.address: 310 Robert T Martinez Jr St, Austin, TX
properties.linked_campuses: Govalle Elementary and Sánchez Elementary (proposed feeders, dropped)
properties.reason: Oct drafts: receive Sánchez and Govalle neighborhood students, boundary changes with Blackshear, and considered as an alternative Montessori site; all dropped.
properties.plan_history: Oct 3/31 drafts only; interim principal Tamsyn Michaels appointed Dec 2025 for January 2026.
properties.community_response: Some Zavala parents objected to insufficient response time on the Montessori idea.

properties.name: Navarro Early College High School
properties.linked_campuses: International High School (proposed program destination, dropped)
properties.reason: Oct 3 draft would have moved International High School to Navarro as a program; final plan closed International HS outright and dropped the Navarro program.
properties.plan_history: Oct 3/31 drafts only.

properties.name: Northeast Early College High School
properties.linked_campuses: International High School (co-located; closing)
properties.reason: Host campus of International High School; current International students may finish at Northeast through graduation with district transportation (December 2025 letter).
properties.plan_history: Oct drafts also proposed boundary changes with LBJ/McCallum/Navarro (dropped Nov 4).

properties.name: Linder Elementary School
properties.reason: Named with Marshall MS as the only campuses in Phase 1 of the post-consolidation boundary realignment (overcrowding relief); open houses Sept 14 and 16, 2026; board vote expected October 2026, effective 2027-28.
properties.plan_history: Oct 3 draft: boundary change with Travis Heights (dropped). Restart plan approved Nov 20, 2025. Aug 2026: Phase 1 boundary scope narrowed to Marshall MS and Linder ES.
properties.demographics_note: Three-F turnaround campus: district-managed restart (ACE model) 2026-27.

properties.name: Burnet Middle School
properties.reason: Not in the consolidation plan (TEA rules barred closing Burnet, Webb and Dobie while their June 2025 turnaround plans were active). Its fifth F triggers state law requiring the commissioner to close the campus or appoint a board of managers; Mayor Watson (Sept 9, 2026) proposed parent petitions to close Burnet and Webb and open a replacement school in the new $158M building.
properties.plan_history: June 26, 2025 ACE restart turnaround plan; excluded from Oct 2025 closure list; Aug 13, 2026 preliminary fifth F; appeal deadline Sept 11, 2026 (district said it would 'likely' appeal, no filing confirmed publicly as of Sept 12); parent-petition deadlines Oct 15 (to superintendent) and Dec 1 (to commissioner); final ratings/decision expected by about Dec 11, 2026.
properties.demographics_note: Five consecutive F ratings (preliminary, Aug 13, 2026; 'one point away' from a D); $158M bond modernization under way on the site.

properties.name: Webb Middle School
properties.address: 601 E St Johns Ave, Austin, TX
properties.reason: Not in the consolidation plan (protected by active turnaround plan); fifth F triggers possible state closure or district takeover; closure via parent petition floated by the mayor in Sept 2026.
properties.plan_history: June 26, 2025 ACE restart turnaround plan; excluded from Oct 2025 closure list; Aug 13, 2026 preliminary fifth F; appeal deadline Sept 11, 2026; petition deadlines Oct 15/Dec 1; decision expected December 2026.
properties.demographics_note: Five consecutive F ratings (preliminary, Aug 13, 2026).

properties.name: Dobie Middle School
properties.reason: Not in the consolidation plan (protected by active turnaround plan); receives the Guerrero Thompson feeder (which absorbs most of Barrington).
properties.plan_history: June 26, 2025 ACE restart turnaround plan; excluded from closure list; D rating Aug 13, 2026 paused its accountability clock.
properties.demographics_note: Broke its four-year F streak with a D in the Aug 2026 preliminary ratings.
